mechanism_narrative: When the FEDFUNDS rate rises by more than 0.25% in a month, the S&P 500 forward 20-day return is expected to turn negative as investors anticipate tighter credit conditions.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS increases by >0.25% in a single month
failure_condition: Over a 12-month window, the 20-day forward return does not fall below the 30th percentile of prior tightening episodes, or FEDFUNDS change is not statistically significant (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in FEDFUNDS for three consecutive months is associated with a positive S&P 500 60-day forward return as market anticipates prolonged easing.
failure_condition: The 60-day forward return does not exceed the 10th percentile of all 60-day windows during periods of three-month FEDFUNDS declines.

mechanism_narrative: When UNRATE falls below 4%, the S&P 500 20-day forward return is positive as labor market slack increases and equity risk premia compress.
failure_condition: In regimes where UNRATE < 4% for at least 30 days, the 20-day forward return is not statistically superior to the prior 20-day average (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in HOUST (household spending) by over 2% in a month coincides with a negative S&P 20-day forward return as excess demand pressures prices and discourages future equity accumulation.
candidate_trigger: HOUST increases by >2% in a single month
failure_condition: Over 6 months, the 20-day forward return does not fall below the 5th percentile during months with HOUST > 2% monthly increase.

mechanism_narrative: When INDPRO rises above 105 (industrial production index), the S&P 60-day forward return is expected to be positive as a signal of growing economic output and reduced recession risk.
failure_condition: In 12 consecutive months with INDPRO > 105, the 60-day forward return does not exceed the 25th percentile of all 60-day windows in non-recessionary regimes.

mechanism_narrative: Concurrent strength in both GDPC1 (GDP) and PAYEMS (employment) for two months creates a positive S&P 20-day forward return as dual demand indicators reduce uncertainty about economic resilience.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 and PAYEMS both increase for 2 consecutive months
failure_condition: During the 2-month dual strength window, the 20-day forward return is not statistically above the 10th percentile (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sudden spike in CPIAUCSL (CPI) of over 0.5% in a month followed by a decline to below 250 triggers a negative S&P 20-day forward return as inflation surprises prompt preemptive selling of equities.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL increases by >0.5% in a month then falls below 250
failure_condition: The 20-day forward return does not turn negative within 5 trading days of the CPI spike, or the spike is not statistically significant (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When UNRATE remains above 5% for three consecutive months in a contractionary regime, the S&P 60-day forward return is negative as persistent labor market tightness raises real rate expectations.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE > 5% for 3 consecutive months in contractionary regime
failure_condition: Over the 60-day window, the forward return does not fall below the 15th percentile during the identified contractionary UNRATE regime.
